title: Uncounted amounts: singular partitive
summary: Use singular partitive after paljon or vähän for a substance or uncounted amount: paljon maitoa — a lot of milk; vähän vettä — a little water. Here vähän means a little of something, rather than a few separate items.
objectives: Use singular partitive after paljon or vähän when talking about an uncounted amount.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use singular partitive after paljon or vähän when talking about an uncounted amount.
Money and substances can be treated as an amount rather than a set of separate items. Paljon means a lot of; vähän means a little in these substance phrases.
The complete noun alternatives are provided when the question assesses case choice.
keyPoints: With paljon or vähän, an uncounted substance or amount takes singular partitive.

steps: With paljon or vähän, an uncounted substance or amount takes singular partitive.
Paljon means “a lot of” and works as the quantity word. paljon is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
maitoa means “milk” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep maito and add -a: maito + a = maitoa.
With paljon or vähän, an uncounted substance or amount takes singular partitive.
Vähän means “a little / few” and works as the quantity word. vähän is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
vettä means “water” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. vesi uses vet- + -tä, written vettä.

kahvia means “coffee” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. This i-word keeps i: kahvi + a = kahvia. The back vowel a determines the ending.
With paljon or vähän, an uncounted substance or amount takes singular partitive.
Vähän means “a little / few” and works as the quantity word. vähän is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
juustoa means “cheese” and works as the singular partitive noun naming counted items or a measured amount. Keep juusto and add -a: juusto + a = juustoa.

commonMistakes: Do not choose plural just because an amount is large.
A little and a lot of use the same noun case here.
